AI is rapidly rewriting the process and paperwork layer for Payroll And Timekeeping Clerks, but on-site judgment and professional experience still rest with people. This article breaks down the specific impact and how to respond.
This work does not suit people who are careless, restless, or intolerant of repetition. Clerks regularly reconcile accounts and find errors, making impatience difficult.
A common path is: begin in administration → become a payroll clerk → calculate payroll independently → become a compensation specialist → transition to HR or finance.
This work suits people who are meticulous, like numbers, and can remain focused. If accurate calculations are your standard, this career offers stability.

Payroll and timekeeping clerks lead the collection and verification of attendance and work hours, coordinate payroll system calculations and deductions, and use rule and system expertise to turn employment data into accurate pay statements.

entries: Payroll and timekeeping clerks lead the collection and verification of attendance and work hours, coordinate payroll system calculations and deductions, and use rule and system expertise to turn employment data into accurate pay statements.

paragraphs: In the morning, collect attendance records from each department and verify hours. At midday, review overtime and leave and identify anomalies. In the afternoon, run the payroll system and calculate deductions. Reconcile accounts, investigate errors, and make several rounds of corrections. Before leaving, finalize pay statements for distribution.

In one sentence: turn work hours into pay. Duties include collecting attendance, verifying data, running payroll, and generating pay statements. The role combines thought with execution and forms the foundation of compensation operations.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), in 2024 about 161,100 payroll and timekeeping clerks were employed. By 2034, employment is projected to fall to 134,200, a net decrease of about 26,900 jobs, with about 13,000 openings per year. In 2026, median annual pay was about $55,300 (BLS OOH, 2026).
